title: Running Click tests in random order and in parallel to find test pollution (tox env 'random')

note.title: Running Click tests in random order and in parallel to find test pollution (tox env 'random')
answers: how do I run click tests in parallel / randomized order
test passes alone but fails in the full suite, how to find leaky tests
what extra tox environments does click have (stress, random)
flaky test detection with pytest-randomly and pytest-xdist
note.body:
Run `tox r -e random`. It is defined in pyproject.toml under [tool.tox.env.random] and installs the `tests-random` dependency group (pytest, pytest-randomly, pytest-xdist). The plain `tests` group does not include these plugins.
The command is `pytest -v --tb=short --numprocesses=auto --basetemp={env_tmp_dir}`, and you can add more pytest args after `--`. `--numprocesses=auto` starts one xdist worker per core. pytest-randomly shuffles the test order on every run, and a test that leaks global state (for example, the leaky test_echo_via_pager mentioned in the PR) then fails some other test at random.
To reproduce an ordering failure, run it again with the seed pytest-randomly prints (`-p randomly -p "randomly_seed=N"` or `-p no:randomly` to turn shuffling off). Seed handling is standard pytest-randomly behaviour; this repo doesn't configure it.
Other extra environments: `tox r -e stress` runs the race-condition stress tests for the test runner's stream lifecycle. A CI workflow, .github/workflows/test-flask.yaml, runs Flask's test suite to catch downstream regressions. All of these are listed in docs/contributing.md.
If you add a dependency group or tox env, update both pyproject.toml and uv.lock (the lock file mirrors the dependency groups).
note.applies: Running or debugging Click's test suite, especially order-dependent or flaky tests
